items.title: US floated NATO membership for Ukraine, Zelenskyy says
paras: Volodymyr Zelenskyy says NATO membership is back on agenda for Ukraine. ( Reuters: Marko Djurica )
The US has raised the possibility of a security framework for Europe to end Russia’s war in Ukraine, President Volodymyr Zelenskyy says.
It's the first time the question of linking NATO membership to territorial concessions has been raised, the president said.
US negotiators raised the idea of Ukraine's potential withdrawal from its eastern region of Donbas in exchange for joining NATO, according to President Volodymyr Zelenskyy.
This is the first time the question of linking NATO membership to territorial concessions has been raised during the talks, the president said.
"That is why I believe NATO is back on the agenda. But you have also heard (Russian President Vladimir) Putin's signals, and this is an extremely difficult conversation."
Mr Putin has long said Ukrainian membership of NATO is a red line for Moscow, citing the issue as one reason for launching Russia's full-blown invasion in 2022.
Mr Zelenskyy reiterated his position that Kyiv was not ready to concede territory.
Mr Zelenskyy and Ireland leader Micheal Martin (right) attend the summit in Dublin. ( Reuters: Cathal McNaughton )

But he also said that if it received a comprehensive package, including security guarantees, the right to a strong and well-funded Ukrainian army and funds to rebuild, he would put the question to a national referendum.

Echoing comments made by European leaders at a summit in Dublin on Friday, Mr Zelenskyy dismissed Russia's call for a broad agreement on European security architecture to be reached before the specifics are agreed on how to end the war in Ukraine.
Mr Zelenskyy also dismissed Mr Putin's suggestion for a local humanitarian ceasefire in Kostiantynivka, saying it reflected Moscow's inability to take the city by force.
Mr Putin wants Uranians to leave Kostiantynivka, Mr Zelenskyy says. ( Reuters )
Civilians there have already had the opportunity to evacuate, he added.
"Putin simply wants us to leave Kostiantynivka so that they can move in and occupy the entire city that way," he said.

Ukraine has given a list of seven or eight other frontline settlements where civilians, including children, are trapped for a potential humanitarian truce but Russia prefers to use them as military targets, Mr Zelenskyy said.
The two days of US-brokered talks between Ukraine and Russia concluded on Wednesday in the Emirati capital without a major breakthrough.
The sides agreed to a prisoner exchange that will involve more than 1,000 people, Mr Zelenskyy said.
The final numbers for the prisoner swap were still under discussion, he added.

US peace envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner had pledged to raise an energy ceasefire with Mr Putin at a meeting in Moscow on Thursday, Zelenskyy said, but there was no news of any progress after their talks.
Mr Zelenskyy met Mr Witkoff and Mr Kushner on Thursday in Ireland after their talks in Moscow.
He said the US negotiators had told him that all sides had agreed for Europe to have a seat at the negotiating table in forthcoming peace talks.
In Abu Dhabi, delegates from Europe — which is now Ukraine's largest financial and military backer — had talks with US and Ukrainian officials but did not sit at the table with Russia.

At the summit in Ireland, EU leaders agreed that Europe's team for any Ukraine peace talks would comprise five major military powers — non-EU member Britain plus France, Germany, Italy and Poland — as well as EU officials.

items.title: 'We're still standing': King Charles jokes with Elton John in birthday clip
paras: King Charles joined Elton John for an episode of his Rocket Hour radio show. ( Supplied: Apple Music/Handout via Reuters )
King Charles joined Sir Elton John for an episode of the singer's radio show which was aired on the monarch's 78th birthday.
The special edition episode of Elton John's Rocket Hour was to celebrate 50 years of The King's Trust.
Britain's King Charles has joked that he and Sir Elton John were "still standing" in a clip recorded for the singer's radio show which was aired on the monarch's 78th birthday.

King Charles had joined Sir John for a special edition of the singer's Elton John's Rocket Hour on Apple Music to celebrate 50 years of The King's Trust and musicians who have supported his youth charity.
During the episode, which was first broadcast on Saturday to coincide with the king's birthday, the pair discussed benefit concerts held in support of the Trust.
This included a Rock Gala held at Wembley Arena in 1986 where Sir Elton performed his 1980s hit, I'm Still Standing.
"I know people in all kinds of circumstances find this song inspiring, not only for its marvellous spirit, but also its message of resilience," King Charles said.
Sir John, who turns 80 in March, replied, "I'm still sitting now, though", prompting laughs from the king.
Both men have suffered well-documented health problems in recent years, with the king still undergoing treatment for cancer and Sir Elton suffering problems with his eyesight.
King Charles and Sir Elton John at the Royal Variety Performance in 2024. ( Reuters: Toby Melville/Pool/File Photo )
When he was the heir, King Charles founded the Prince's Trust in 1976 using his Royal Navy severance pay to help disadvantaged young people prepare for work, find jobs or start businesses.
The charity says it has supported more than one million young people since its launch.

"Music has always been at the heart of The Prince's, and now The King's Trust," King Charles said, adding that the program offered a chance to showcase performers who had supported the charity and newer artists it had helped launch.
The pair recalled benefit concerts stretching from Wembley Arena's rock galas in the 1980s to shows in Hyde Park and at the Royal Albert Hall.
Among them is British rock band Muse, which received a grant to buy sound equipment when it performed under its former name Rocket Baby Dolls.
The group later held a sold-out Royal Albert Hall concert in aid of the Trust in 2018, Buckingham Palace said in a statement.
"If you champion a young artist and show you believe in them, it makes all the difference," Sir Elton said.
Sir Elton received the Order of the Companions of Honour from Charles, then Prince of Wales, at Windsor Castle in 2021 for services to music and charity.
One of the best-selling artists of all time, with hits including "Goodbye Yellow Brick Road", "Rocket Man" and "Your Song", Sir Elton was knighted by Queen Elizabeth in 1998.
Rocket Hour is a weekly show that has aired globally on Apple Music 1 since 2015.

items.title: Change or go extinct
paras: During February this year, Angus Taylor gave his first press conference as the new Liberal leader, presenting a stark warning that the Liberals must ‘change or die’. Nine months later, the party’s behaviour seems set on the latter, with their idea of ‘change’ struggling to compete against One Nation and its rising popularity.

That rise is no accident. It is a result of the Liberals refusing to acknowledge that One Nation is no longer just a ‘nothing party’ but instead is replacing them. Rather than face this, their strategy seems to include positioning themselves as the pragmatic counter to One Nation, hoping it collapses so the Liberals can win back their old voters.

I remember attending CPAC Australia last month. Whenever a Liberal MP spoke, they consistently framed their party as the ‘right’ and more reliable party. It was obviously a ploy aimed at One Nation, almost in a manner that ignored that they were an actual political party worth considering.

In my view, Angus Taylor’s speech illustrated this attitude, stating: ‘A changed and better Liberal Party – together with the Nationals – remains the most credible alternative government to deliver the change our country desperately needs.’
MPs like Dan Tehan also said, ‘The Liberals and Nationals will scrap Net Zero and prioritise cheaper power.’

It’s a pitch that assumes the Liberals are the only conservatives on offer, when One Nation is already making the same promise. Though Taylor didn’t avoid Pauline Hanson altogether, he did take a subtle side-swipe, saying, ‘Strong government isn’t built around one figure. It’s built around a plan and a credible team.’

The Liberals’ attitude, resembling a type of elitist self-pride mindset, has not gotten them anywhere. Recent RedBridge/Accent polling has put One Nation at 28 per cent and the Liberals/Nationals at 25 per cent.

I believe the Liberal Party sees their key selling point as pragmatism, based on the belief that their policies will carry them to victory. Taylor emphasised that by saying, ‘There’s much work the Coalition must do to win your confidence. But with the policies I’ve announced tonight – and the vision I’ve outlined – I hope you can begin to believe again.’

The reason this hasn’t landed with voters is that voters know they have a new alternative conservative party that challenges them. But once again the Liberals fail to come to terms with the fact that One Nation isn’t the party it was 20 years ago when it was primarily a populist force without strong ‘policies’.

An article recently released by Ronald Mizen in the Australian Financial Review echoes this shift, highlighting how One Nation is attracting ‘seriously deep-pocketed backers’ – something that doesn’t happen to a party that is merely, as many critics like to suggest, a ‘fringe party’. The article highlighted how Chris Taylor, One Nation’s new chief of staff and known as a banking lobby heavyweight, and Pauline Hanson sat down with people from think tanks, alongside investors and economists. The article went on to suggest that one major investor, who was apparently reluctant to take the meeting, was glad he ended up doing it, stating, ‘She’s going to be a bit of a vessel for many, many ideas.’ The article further highlights how Chris Taylor has ‘recruited two other colleagues from the major bank lobby group, Maxwell Pryor and Alexander Bourne’. The Liberals have tried to position themselves as the only party with the serious policies and governance. That isn’t and won’t hold up for much longer, as what One Nation is starting to assert with the recent backing from credible sources shakes what Liberals have been leaning on.

This decline in trust for the Liberal Party isn’t anything new, but has been weakening since late in Tony Abbott’s term. Whilst the rise of right-wing third-party systems, like Reform UK and National Rally from France, has picked up around the globe, all of them share the rhetoric and policy ideas that traditional conservative parties have ignored or failed to put into practice. The failure of the Liberals in Australia shows this more specifically, in the clear bubble they have put themselves in, which consists of not listening to voters.

That internal bubble is dramatically different from One Nation, where in the AFR article the anonymous investor stated that, ‘If people put good ideas to her, she’s receptive.’ The Liberals, by contrast, act like an out-of-touch party and think they know what’s best, which was evident when the loudest cheer at CPAC went to Pauline Hanson, who said One Nation ‘will work with the Liberals and Nationals’. An hour later, Taylor was booed for side-stepping the question after being asked multiple times if he would work with One Nation. Angus was told what the voters wanted, but he didn’t listen.

The strategy that the Liberals are using should make sense considering One Nation’s rise and fall and dramatic rise again, with candidates and policies traditionally being in some ways unqualified and/or on the fringe side of the booted old Liberal members. That strategy doesn’t work in 2026, with Pauline Hanson and One Nation not only getting credibility, but also establishing themselves as, if not the most important player in Australian politics.
As the popularity and credibility of One Nation continue to rise, it does not gain the Liberal Party any more votes from the already defected traditional Liberal voters.
Saying you hear the concerns of Australians does not win votes when the Liberals’ actions continually go against what voters want.

Although One Nation still needs to prove itself capable of governing, the Liberals’ mentality shows no sign of changing. The Liberals’ strategy of hoping One Nation will fall, and believing it is just a minor party with no influence or pull, is what will get them walloped, not just in polling but at the election. Taylor warned that the party must change or die. If it keeps waiting for its rival to collapse, it may be the one that does.

items.title: Reserve Bank of India imposes monetary penalty on One Mobikwik Systems Limited
paras: Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has, by an order dated November 06, 2026, imposed a monetary penalty of ₹9.00 lakh (Rupees Nine Lakh only) on One Mobikwik Systems Limited (the company) for non-compliance with certain provisions of the directions issued by RBI on ‘Prepaid Payment lnstruments (PPIs)’ and ‘Fraud reporting’. This penalty has been imposed in exercise of powers conferred on RBI under the provisions of section 30(1) read with section 26(6) of the Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2007. The statutory inspection of the company was conducted by RBI with reference to its operations for the period from June 2025 to March 2026. Based on supervisory findings of non-compliance with RBI directions and related correspondence in that regard, a notice was issued to the company advising it to show cause as to why penalty should not be imposed on it for its failure to comply with the said RBI directions. After considering the company’s reply to the notice, additional submissions made by it and oral submissions made during the personal hearing, RBI found that the following charges against the company were sustained, warranting imposition of monetary penalty: the company had allowed fund transfer by certain PPI holders to non-pre-registered beneficiaries beyond the prescribed limit. the company failed to report certain frauds within the prescribed timeline. The action is based on deficiencies in regulatory compliance and is not intended to pronounce upon the validity of any transaction or agreement entered into by the company with its customers. Further, imposition of monetary penalty is without prejudice to any other action that may be initiated by RBI against the company. (Brij Raj) Chief General Manager Press Release: 2026-2027/1496

items.title: ED arrests six persons in cross-border drugs smuggling network
paras: Join our Whatsapp channel New Delhi [India], October 22 (ANI): The Enforcement Directorate ( ED ) has arrested six persons in connection with an investigation under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA) case linked to a cross-border drug smuggling network, the agency said on Tuesday. ED 's Delhi unit arrested these accused in different operations launched on October 11, October 18 and October 20. The arrested accused are identified as Lovejit Singh alias Labba, Manjeet Singh alias Manna, Prabhjit Singh, Gurjot Singh, Ramandeep Singh, and Gurpreet Singh. "A major drug trafficking operation involving smuggling of heroin from Afghanistan into India was unearthed during investigation," said the ED in a statement. The PMLA investigation was initiated on the basis of seizure of 293.81 kg of heroin from containers imported by Sandhu Exports at Nhava Sheva Port by the Directorate of Revenue Intelligence and seizure of 352.71 kg of heroin from two vehicles and a flat in Faridabad, Haryana, by the Delhi Police Special Cell. Thus, a total of 646.52 kg of heroin has been seized so far. ED investigation revealed that the arrested persons, Lovejit Singh, Manjeet Singh, Ramandeep Singh, Gurjot Singh, Gurpreet Singh and Prabhjit Singh, coordinated the smuggling, storage and distribution of heroin across Punjab, Haryana, and Delhi.

"These individuals were key members of a syndicate that smuggled heroin from Afghanistan and Iran, concealing them within shipments of talc stone and gypsum powder," said the ED . Accused persons incorporated Sandhu Exports, a front company owned by Prabhjit Singh, to carry out the smuggling of drugs, informed the federal agency. ED uncovered the highly sophisticated heroin smuggling and money laundering network where identification of multiple bank accounts, cash transactions, and operational expenses by the accused has been made. "Accused disguised the origin of the illicit funds, which were further layered and integrated into seemingly legitimate financial activities. It was also revealed that the syndicate did not make any payments to Afghan suppliers until the drugs were sold in local markets." Further, the agency said the accused used cash payments to purchase multiple vehicles including Toyota Fortuner, Etios and Hyundai Verna etc in second hand market for trafficking from the storage Hubs to further distribution. The ED investigation revealed that cash was used for the purchase of high-end smartphones and encrypted communication apps were used to coordinate smuggling activities. "Drugs smuggled from Iran and Afghanistan used to be imported via the Nava Sheva port in Mumbai, later stored at a rented godown in Shivpuri, Madhya Pradesh and further distributed for local supply in parts of Delhi, Punjab and Haryana. Transportation was carried out in lesser quantities of 10 kg to prevent detection by law enforcement agencies. Earlier, a property in Jandoli Village (Rajpura, Punjab), multiple bank accounts in the names of accused persons, and fixed deposits have been attached by ED ," added the agency. (ANI)

items.title: Asia's Largest Mindfulness India Summit 2024 Marks a New Era for Corporate Culture and Personal Well-being with the Inau
paras: Join our Whatsapp channel PNN Mumbai (Maharashtra) [India], October 22: The Mindfulness India Summit 2024, an initiative by the Mindful Science Centre, presented by HSBC and supported by CII Leadership and HR Committee, successfully concluded its two-day event on October 17 and 18, 2024, establishing new benchmarks in corporate culture and personal well-being. With over 40 international and national experts addressing mindfulness, emotional intelligence, and neuroscience, the summit highlighted how these principles are essential in transforming leadership, enhancing employee engagement, and fostering sustainable well-being within organizations. The evolving workplace landscape, particularly the increasing role of AI, requires a renewed focus on human-centric leadership and emotional resilience. The summit provided a platform for forward-thinking leaders to explore how mindfulness can effectively bridge this gap, ensuring both corporate excellence and employee well-being . The summit featured MasterChef Sanjeev Kapoor as the Chief Guest, who shared how mindful leadership has played a pivotal role in building his culinary empire. Along with Chris Ruane, Ex MP British Parliament and Chair of Mindfulness Initiative UK, J N Behl and Global Holistic Health Guru Mickey Mehta, Kapoor also launched Manish Behl's new book "Observe - 101 Mindfulness Practices", a guide designed to make mindfulness accessible for both professionals and individuals in their everyday lives. Behl, a global mindfulness expert and founder of the Mindful Science Centre, shared, "With this book, I want to demystify mindfulness and make it accessible to everyone. Mindfulness is not a complex or distant concept, but a practical tool for reducing stress, improving focus, and fostering deeper connections in both personal and professional settings." The Mindfulness India Summit 2024 has successfully proven that mindfulness is no longer a luxury but a necessity in modern corporate structures. By adopting mindfulness practices, organizations are not only creating more compassionate work environments but are also enhancing their overall performance and sustainability in a world increasingly shaped by technological and emotional complexity. The 2 days also saw the launch of Mindfulness Impact Awards, to honor organizations and individuals who have integrated mindfulness into their corporate structures and personal lives. These awards reflect the growing recognition that workplace culture directly affects employee productivity, creativity, and overall well-being. Manish Behl, founder of the awards, explained, "Corporate success today goes beyond profit; it's about fostering environments where employees thrive mentally, emotionally, and physically. Our vision with these awards is to inspire a deeper integration of mindfulness in corporate cultures worldwide. By recognizing these pioneers, we hope these awards inspire companies and individuals to further integrate mindfulness into their environments, ultimately fostering happier, more productive workplaces, communities, and a more compassionate world." The awards were designed to acknowledge champions of mindfulness across categories, recognizing those who incorporate mindful practices to improve workplace culture, employee engagement, and societal impact. Winners ranged from corporate giants like Aditya Birla Group and Accenture to global educators and community leaders. Award Winners Include: - Entrepreneur: Mickey Mehta (India) - Commitment: Aditya Birla Group, Accenture (India) - Champions: IPG Mediabrands (India) - Communities: HPCL (India) - Champions: Hincolas (India)

items.title: Indian students in Kazan delighted as PM Modi arrives for BRICS Summit
paras: Join our Whatsapp channel Kazan [ Russia ], October 22 (ANI): Indian students in Kazan , Russia , are happy and excited about Prime Minister Narendra Modi's arrival at Hotel Korston , as he attends the 16th BRICS Summit . Notably, PM Narendra Modi on Tuesday touched down in Kazan city of Russia to participate in the 16th BRICS Summit and received a warm welcome. He is here to attend the 16th BRICS Summit , being held under the Chairmanship of Russia . To welcome PM Modi , students from India studying in Russia also sang a welcome song as they awaited PM Modi 's arrival at Hotel Korston . An Indian student from Pune, Saniya said that the students are quite excited to greet PM Modi . "Maybe we will get the opportunity (to meet PM Modi ) as many students are here (at Hotel Korston )... We are very excited. We are lucky to have this opportunity and we are happy to see him," she told ANI. An Indian student from Bihar, Shaurya Pratap said, "We are very happy to welcome PM Modi and we have prepared a song for him and we hope he likes it." Surbhi from Delhi said, "I have been here in Kazan since 2019 and today, we are going to sing a song for PM Modi and we are very excited about that." Parul, a final-year medical student, who has been in Kazan for the last five years told ANI, "We are really grateful that we got this opportunity to welcome our dear Prime Minister." Arti Pawar from Maharashtra said, "I have been living here for the past three years. I am very happy that PM Modi is coming here." Mrunmayi from Nagpur, Maharashtra said, "All the students here are quite enthusiastic as PM is going to come soon. We are too much delighted to welcome him." Meanwhile, ISKCON volunteers - from the Russia n and Indian communities were seen chanting 'Hare Krishna, Hare Ram' ahead of PM Modi 's arrival. While speaking with ANI, Sergoy, an ISKCON volunteer, said, "'Hare Krishna is a Mahamantra. This visit of PM Modi to Kazan , Russia is an important one for us. We are happy." Another ISKCON volunteer said, "We want to welcome PM Modi here in Kazan . It's a great honour for us to welcome him here We are very excited to see him." A Russia n citizen, Alexander said that the people there will welcome PM Modi by singing a song and that he is happy with PM Modi 's visit to Kazan . He said, "We have made a banner and we will also sing a song to welcome PM Modi ... I returned from India just two days back and directly came from Delhi to Kazan to see PM Modi . I am very happy that he is coming to Russia ." Notably, ahead of his departure to Russia , PM Modi shared a post on X and wrote, "Leaving for Kazan , Russia , to take part in the BRICS Summit . India attaches immense importance to BRICS, and I look forward to extensive discussions on a wide range of subjects. I also look forward to meeting various leaders there." The Prime Minister's office in a statement quoted PM Modi as saying, "I am departing today on a two-day visit to Kazan at the invitation of H.E. Mr. Vladimir Putin, President of the Russia n Federation, to attend the 16th BRICS Summit ." "India values the close cooperation within BRICS which has emerged as an important platform for dialogue and discussion on issues concerning the global developmental agenda, reformed multilateralism, climate change, economic cooperation, building resilient supply chains, promoting cultural and people to people connect, among others," PM Modi said. The statement further said that the expansion of BRICS with the addition of new members last year has added to its inclusivity and agenda for the global good. "Building upon the Annual Summit held in July 2024 in Moscow, my visit to Kazan will further reinforce the Special and Privileged Strategic Partnership between India and Russia . I look forward to meeting other leaders from BRICS as well," the PMO statement said. The 16th BRICS Summit in Kazan is being held under the chairmanship of Russia from October 22-24. During his visit, PM Modi is also expected to hold bilateral meetings with his counterparts from BRICS member countries and invited leaders in Kazan . The Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) said, "The Summit, themed 'Strengthening Multilateralism for Just Global Development and Security,' will provide an important platform for leaders to discuss key global issues." It further said, "The Summit will offer a valuable opportunity to assess the progress of initiatives launched by BRICS and to identify potential areas for future collaboration." This visit marks, PM Modi 's second visit to Russia this year. He travelled to Moscow in July to attend the 22nd India- Russia Annual Summit where he held a bilateral meeting with President Putin. He was also conferred with Russia 's highest civilian award, the Order of St. Andrew the Apostle at the Kremlin in Moscow. BRIC, as a formal grouping, started after the meeting of the Leaders of Russia , India and China in St Petersburg on the margins of G8 Outreach Summit in 2006. The grouping was formalized during the first meeting of BRIC Foreign Ministers on the margins of UNGA in New York in 2006. The first BRIC Summit was held in Russia 's Yekaterinburg in 2009. It was agreed to expand BRIC into BRICS with the inclusion of South Africa at the BRIC Foreign Ministers' meeting in New York in 2010. South Africa attended the 3rd BRICS Summit in Sanya in 2011. A further expansion of BRICS took place in 2024 with five new members - Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran, Saudi Arabia, and the United Arab Emirates. (ANI)

items.title: "Singapore plays key role in Act-East policy": Rajnath Singh at India-Singapore Defence Ministers' Dialogue
paras: Join our Whatsapp channel New Delhi [ India ], October 22 (ANI): Dr. Ng Eng Hen , Singapore 's Minister of Defence , has begun his three-day visit to India . As part of his visit, Dr. Hen co-chaired the sixth India - Singapore Defence Ministers' Dialogue in New Delhi, with his India n counterpart Rajnath Singh . The Summit began on Tuesday morning, with India n Defence Minister Rajnath Singh welcoming the Singapore delegation warmly. He noted that the strategic partnership the two countries share is a "testimony of increasing closeness between our countries." Singh said, " The meeting is happening at a time when India marks the decade of India 's Act in Policy, in which Singapore has played a key role in promoting economic cooperation, cultural ties, and developed strategic connectivity with country institutions." Building upon Singh's remarks, Dr. Ng Eng Hen said, "You reminded us that this is the 10th year since your Act East Policy. From Singapore 's perspective, India has always been part of the East. Whether you choose to act or look, we consider you part of the area." He said that while remembering the history of Singapore , India has been an important partner. " When we started the Singapore armed forces, one of the countries that we asked early on to see whether they could help us was India ." Hen highlighted that such historical memoirs serve as important reminders and "reflects how we feel that India is very part of our area. We are delighted that our ten years of bilateral relations have been very much improved in defence and all-round strategic partnership." Hen also thanked PM Modi for visiting Singapore earlier this year and noted that the visit was an excellent meeting. A day before, the Ministry of Defence had announced the sixth India - Singapore Defence Ministers' Dialogue in New Delhi on October 22, 2024. The release noted that between India and Singapore , "The engagements have diversified to include wide-ranging contacts between the Services, military-to-military exchanges, high-level visits, capacity building and training programs, cooperation in UN Peacekeeping, ship visits and bilateral exercises." Inaugurated in 2016, the India - Singapore Defence Ministers' Dialogue is a key platform to strengthen bilateral defence cooperation between Singapore and India . The fifth edition of the Defence Ministers' Dialogue took place in January 2021 through virtual teleconference. During the meeting, the two parties showed confidence in the outcomes of the meeting that would result in providing impetus to the entire spectrum of the bilateral engagement as well as to the regional security architecture. (ANI)

items.title: "India matters most for future of planet" says British High Commissioner Lindy Cameron
paras: Join our Whatsapp channel New Delhi [India], October 22 (ANI): In recent times when climate change has become a pressing issue with countries across the world being ravaged due to climate catastrophes, it becomes imperative to discuss and deliberate upon global actions that can help the world rise up and meet these challenges. At the NDTV World Summit's a discussion was held on the theme, "India Matters The Most For Future Of Planet". Participants in the discussion included Erik Solheim, Former Minister of Climate and the Environment of Norway; Lindy Cameron , British High Commissioner to India; Shishir Priyadarshi, President Chintan Research Foundation; Harjeet Singh, Global Engagement Director, Fossil Fuel Non-Proliferation Treaty Initiative. "India is the country that matters the most for the future of the planet and climate change. India's ambition for development should not in any way be constrained by the responsibilities of the planet," Lindy Cameron , British High Commissioner to India, emphasised. She noted that the UK is committed towards the Multilateral Development Banks (MDB) reforms, technology and research support in India to aid the efforts. "Every dollar invested in resilient infrastructure pays 4 times over," said Cameron. "Lived experience of climate emergencies helps people to understand why their government needs to take policy action now," she added. Further talking about the need for urgent government action, Harjeet Singh, Global Engagement Director, Fossil Fuel Non-Proliferation Treaty Initiative said, "Series of disasters affecting both developed and developing countries are serving as a wake-up call. As rich countries will get more and more affected by climate change which they did not imagine till a couple of years ago, most vulnerable countries are going to be struggling with impacts who also have very less capacity to deal with it. India is taking a leadership role in the global fight against climate change. Initiatives such as Global Biofuels Alliance, International Solar Alliance, and Coalition for Disaster Resilient Infrastructure are some efforts taken by India in recent years to manage the climate crisis. (ANI)

items.title: "No shortage of oil in world and prices should hopefully come down", says Hardeep Singh Puri
paras: Join our Whatsapp channel New Delhi [India], October 22 (ANI): Hardeep Singh Puri, Minister for Petroleum and Natural Gas on Tuesday said that there is no shortage of oil in the world and prices will come down soon, answering the question of the recent upswing in crude oil prices. Speaking to the media, the Union Minister cited global factors such as the war in the Middle East and voluntary cuts in oil production which are influencing the oil prices in the global market. He said, "It depends on global factors. One thing is very clear, there is no shortage of oil in the world...Today, more and more oil is coming on the market...There are other factors like geopolitical tensions. So, there is no shortage of oil but if there is tension in one part of the world, then the freight cost, and insurance freight cost will go up. Today, let us all hope that better sense prevails, that call for peace that our Prime Minister has been making from every forum...There is more than enough oil in the world and prices should hopefully come down. That's my expectation..." "If there's tension in one part of the world, then the cost of, if you have to take a longer route, then the cost of the freight cost, the insurance rate cost, that will go up...There's more than enough oil in the world, and prices should hopefully come down," he commented in his personal capacity.

The union minister said many countries such as Brazil, and Guayana among others are coming with their oil. Citing the stable prices in the last 3 years, the minister said that the government is taking every possible step to ensure stable oil prices. "Central government at every stage has stepped in to cushion and bring the prices down from November 2021 to May 2022. Now there are some global factors. The cost at the retail point is determined by the cost of the barrel in the international market plus the cost of transportation, freight, insurance, retailers, refining cost and margin, then dealers, margin, etc. We are solving all the problems we can, now you tell the global community to hold and bring them down," he added. This comes after oil prices rose nearly 2 per cent on Monday, reclaiming major losses from last week's sell-off. Brent crude features upped by $1.44, or 1.97 per cent in the afternoon. Earlier this month, Puri had said that the country is well-prepared to meet its growing energy demands, with a diverse range of oil sources. Speaking on the availability of oil in the global market, Puri emphasised that India has expanded its procurement base, moving from 27 suppliers to 39. (ANI)

items.title: India is the top market for investment globally: Mark Mobius
paras: Join our Whatsapp channel New Delhi [India], October 22 (ANI): Mark Mobius, Founder of Mobius Capital Partners LLP , and an ace investor with expertise in emerging markets said, India's is the top stock market globally where he would like to invest. In an exclusive interview with ANI, the octagenarian said, "India would have to come first when I think about investment," Mobius stated, "Of course, India would have to be the first choice. Then, I would probably look at Taiwan. It's a Chinese society, but it's a free society and they're doing very well. Now we're beginning to see China rise again. There will be some interesting companies in China, but still, India remains our top pick." Mobius highlighted technology as his favorite sector to invest in India. "In the future, I believe there's going to be significant growth in hardware technology. As you know, India is already strong in software technology, but moving forward, hardware manufacturing will gain momentum here in India," he said. Discussing India's semiconductor infrastructure, Mobius mentioned that it is already developing. "Many of the world's large semiconductor companies already have software development operations in India, employing thousands of software engineers. The next step, of course, is hardware. Soon, we'll see large semiconductor manufacturing plants. The scale of investment we're talking about isn't in the millions, but billions of dollars, to produce the most advanced semiconductors in the world." Mobius also fondly remembered Ratan Tata, who passed away this month. "I met him many years ago and found him to be a very friendly, humble, and insightful person. I was deeply saddened to hear about his passing. I considered him one of the great Indian entrepreneurs of the century," Mobius added. Earlier on Monday, Mark Mobius, speaking at the NDTV World Summit 2024, reiterated he was bullish on India's real estate and semiconductor sectors, as he outlined the potential of these two key industries. In the semiconductor space, he said fabrication companies (fabs) will come here because India has got the population and the labour force. The octagenarian believes India will become "the leader" of the semiconductor industry. The government has so far approved five semiconductor units in India, of which construction in two sites is on, and soon the work in the other three will start. The companies have already made a cumulative investment of almost Rs 1.5 lakh crore. While talking about the parameters he looks at while investing in companies, Mobius said he looks at the growth of earnings in companies, along with the return on capital invested, and the quality of management. Asked about his investment advice to his "younger self," Mobius said, "Don't be in a rush, and study carefully". He added that one has to listen to the market. (ANI)

items.title: James Webb telescope finds ice older than the star it orbits
paras: On ice James Webb telescope finds ice older than the star it orbits Radiation and collisions reshape the planetary building materials.

13 ... ... ... A ground-based telescope's view of Beta Pictoris. Credit: ESO/A.-M. Lagrange Et Al. A ground-based telescope's view of Beta Pictoris. Credit: ESO/A.-M. Lagrange Et Al. Text settings Story text Size Small Standard Large Width * Standard Wide Links Standard Orange * Subscribers only Learn more Minimize to nav Beta Pictoris is a young star, roughly 20 million years old, and located about 64 light-years away from Earth. It is surrounded by a vast disk of dust and rubble where planets are still forming—astronomers have already found three. In a new Science study, a team led by Sarah Betti, an astronomer at the Space Telescope Science Institute in Baltimore, used the James Webb Space Telescope to look for ice in this disk. Researchers found both water and carbon dioxide ice.

The water ice is glassy rather than crystalline, and it is mixed with carbon dioxide in roughly the same proportions we see in comets of our own Solar System. This suggests ingredients necessary to form water-rich worlds might be common around young stars.

Beta Pictoris is one of the best studied stars in the sky. Its disk was among the first ever imaged, back in 1984, and we see it almost exactly edge-on, which makes it a natural laboratory for studying how planetary systems grow. It’s what astronomers call a debris disk, where the dust is constantly replenished by collisions among comets and planetesimals, small bodies that are the building blocks of planets.

The outer parts of the disk are far enough from the star that water and other volatile molecules should freeze into solid ice. The disk holds a large reservoir of carbon monoxide gas, which ultraviolet light from the star should destroy within 50 to 300 years. For that gas to still be there, something must keep replenishing it—most likely it’s released from ice when volatile-rich comets collide. The properties of the planet Beta Pictoris b also suggest it formed from ice-rich material.

Yet despite plenty of reasons to suspect the system is full of ice, earlier searches have failed to find it. Attempts to detect water vapor found nothing, and a search for the telltale dip that water ice leaves in starlight at a wavelength of 3 micrometers also failed.

According to theoretical models, ultraviolet radiation from the star can destroy small grains of pure ice faster than collisions can produce them. On the other hand, grains of dirty ice, mixed with other molecules, should survive longer.

Betti and her colleagues observed Beta Pictoris on December 7, 2023, using Webb’s Near Infrared Spectrograph (NIRSpec). They operated it in a mode that records a full spectrum, from 0.6 to 5.2 micrometers, for every point in the image. After subtracting the overwhelming glare of the star, the team measured how much starlight the disk’s dust reflects at each wavelength to look for the fingerprints of ices.

Water ice absorbs light strongly near 3 micrometers, while carbon dioxide ice absorbs either at 4.27 micrometers or 4.39 micrometers when it contains the heavier carbon-13 isotope. The team first mapped the water ice features across the disk and found they were strikingly uniform. They then extracted detailed spectra from two spots on opposite sides of the star, each roughly 100 astronomical units out.

Both spectra showed water and carbon dioxide ices, the latter in both its common form and the rarer carbon-13 version. But the shape of those features turned out to tell us more than the fact they were there.

The carbon dioxide features were shifted slightly toward shorter wavelengths and were much broader than those of pure carbon dioxide ice measured in the lab. The team says in the paper that this is how carbon dioxide behaves when its molecules are trapped inside water ice. In other words, the two ices aren’t sitting side by side as separate grains—they are thoroughly mixed, which makes it the kind of dirty ice that models suggested could survive the star’s ultraviolet radiation.

The team calculated that there is slightly more than one carbon dioxide molecule for every 10 water molecules, meaning it’s about 11 percent of the ice. That falls within the 2.5 to 30 percent range measured in Solar System comets and the 7 to 20 percent seen in the ice of disks around other newborn stars. It means the ices of Beta Pictoris may have formed through the same processes as in our own Solar System, building up on dust grains in cold, dense, water-rich clouds during the earliest stages of star formation.

The structure of the water ice also pointed in this direction. When water freezes at moderate temperatures, its molecules settle into an orderly crystal lattice, and crystalline ice produces a sharp peak in the spectrum just above 3 micrometers. That peak was absent at Beta Pictoris. The ice is almost entirely amorphous, a disordered, glass-like solid that forms when water molecules freeze so fast and so cold that they stick wherever they land. The team estimates that less than 7 percent of the water ice in the system is crystalline, which is somewhat surprising.

Models predicted that ice in debris disks should mostly be crystalline. For amorphous ice to stay in that form, it has to remain colder than about 100 Kelvin, or minus 173° Celsius. Otherwise, something has to keep breaking up its crystal structure, such as high-energy ultraviolet light, cosmic rays, or particles streaming from the star. Either way, the researchers concluded the ice most likely formed in the interstellar medium, long before the planets of Beta Pictoris began to take shape.
The remaining question was how the icy grains got spread so evenly across the disk.

The team argues that this even ice distribution requires frequent collisions among planetesimals. Each collision would release fresh icy dust, including ice that had been buried and protected deep inside the colliding bodies, replenishing what the starlight destroys. We already have evidence that such collisions do happen. Earlier infrared images revealed a curved, lopsided streak of dust in the southwestern arm of the disk, thought to be debris from a violent collision a little less than halfway out from the star.

Betti’s team’s findings support the idea that the disk’s carbon monoxide gas comes from colliding icy bodies and offer an explanation of how ice can survive in an environment constantly exposed to ultraviolet light. What the team could not do is determine exactly how much crystalline ice is present or rule out other molecules hiding in the mixture.

But if a young planetary system 64 light-years away may have started with much the same icy ingredients as ours, then primordial, interstellar ice might be a common ingredient of planetary systems in general. This means the raw materials for water-rich, potentially habitable worlds might be common, too.

items.title: Winemakers are learning that conservation can be good for business
paras: Wine and roses Winemakers are learning that conservation can be good for business Healthy soils, native plants, and fewer chemicals are helping vineyards adapt.

5 ... ... ... This vineyard, seen through an electric fence, relies on cover crops in South Africa’s Western Cape region. Credit: Hannah Herrero This vineyard, seen through an electric fence, relies on cover crops in South Africa’s Western Cape region. Credit: Hannah Herrero Text settings Story text Size Small Standard Large Width * Standard Wide Links Standard Orange * Subscribers only Learn more Minimize to nav More than 500 vineyards are scattered across the slopes and valleys of South Africa’s Western Cape , one of the world’s most biologically diverse landscapes. The region produces about 90 percent of South Africa’s wine , but winemakers there are increasingly struggling with drought, excessive heat and erratic rainfall.

Temperatures in the region have risen 1.5 to 2 times faster than the global average over the past five decades. And extreme storms have become more intense as climate variability increases. The late 2010s brought a significant challenge for winemakers, as three years of severe drought placed vineyards under intense stress and reduced grape production.
As climate variability places increasing pressure on grape production, many wine producers are building on sustainability measures that have long been part of vineyard management.

We are a team of geographers and sustainability scientists who study environmental change , environmental health, conservation, agriculture and land management. Our team wanted to better understand how farmers in South Africa’s wine-producing regions are responding as a range of environmental and economic pressures rise. We talked with growers, conservation practitioners and wine industry experts in the Western Cape and analyzed how 107 vineyards , about 20% of the total, were using sustainable land stewardship practices to adapt.

In many agricultural landscapes, production and conservation goals are frequently viewed as competing priorities . But our research found that many vineyard operators in the Western Cape see long-term stewardship and conservation of soil and wildlife habitat as essential strategies for business success.

The Western Cape is home to the Cape Floral Region , a global biodiversity hot spot. It includes fynbos , a unique biome containing thousands of endemic plant species, including types of proteas , ericas and restios that are found nowhere else on Earth.

Sustainability certification and conservation programs, such as World Wildlife Fund Conservation Champions , have helped encourage vineyards to protect biodiversity in the region. Many growers use these sustainability certifications to increase their wine’s marketability. But we found they have also embraced conservation for how it can benefit their vineyards. Rather than viewing conservation as land taken out of production, many said they see it supporting the ecological processes essential to their business.

The majority of South Africa’s vineyards today participate in the Integrated Production of Wine certification system, created by the South African wine industry and researchers in 1998 to reduce environmental harm. The system sets standards governing pesticide use, water management, wastewater treatment and environmental stewardship. It also uses independent auditing of participating farms and wineries to ensure those claiming certification meet the standards.

To manage the water supplies their vineyards depend on, growers described restoring native vegetation , including the removal of alien species, along waterways and reducing erosion to protect wetlands and rivers. Research shows that healthy natural systems can improve water retention in the soil and contribute to the overall resilience of the landscape in the face of more extreme climate conditions.

To boost their soil’s health, some growers are planting cover crops , such as legumes , cereals like oats and rye, and brassicas such as radish and mustard, between vine rows. Growers broadly described using cover crops, compost, mulching and other practices to improve soil structure and increase organic matter in the soil. Cover crops require maintenance and can provide habitat for pests, but research shows that the right cover crops, when well maintained, can benefit vineyards by reducing erosion and increasing water retention and nutrients in the soil.

Several producers also described efforts to reduce their reliance on chemical pesticides, which is beneficial not only for the environment but also their businesses as chemical costs continue to rise . We heard about vineyards that monitor pest populations closely and respond in targeted ways rather than using pesticides broadly.

Some growers encourage beneficial insects and manage habitats that support natural pest control . The creation of habitats for natural pest predators can reduce the overall disease risk too. While chemical treatments remain part of many vineyard operations, growers reported increasing interest in other approaches that prevent disease and pest outbreaks, such as pruning, to reduce their total chemical use.

Sustainable practices like these are well established in South Africa’s wine industry, but our interviews suggest their use has been expanding in recent years. Rather than focusing solely on treating problems after they arise, these approaches emphasize prevention, monitoring and ecological balance.
The stewardship practices we observed in South Africa are investments in long-term business resilience for many growers.

Many of the wine producers we interviewed described facing rising costs and market uncertainty. Exports, labor and chemicals are all expensive. They emphasized that maintaining healthy soils, conserving water and reducing vulnerability to drought and disease are essential to keeping their vineyards productive.

As concerns about drought, climate pressures and profitability rise, the area in vineyard production in South Africa has also decreased . Several growers described diversifying their business models and even switching crops to make their businesses more resilient to hotter, drier conditions.
Farmers around the world are confronting the realities of a changing climate . Our research shows that effective solutions can come from recognizing the interconnectedness of nature and production.
The experience of South Africa’s winegrowers shows that farms can be managed more sustainably when they’re seen as part of larger ecological systems.
Students Zoe Van der Walt , Jack Spining and Dryver Finch contributed to this article.

Hannah V. Herrero is Associate Professor of Geography & Sustainability and Director of Sustainability at University of Tennessee ; Erin L. Bunting is Assistant Professor of Geography at Michigan State University ; Jane Southworth is Professor of Geography at University of Florida ; Jason K. Blackburn is Professor of Geography at University of Florida ; and Stephanie Insalaco-Wyner is Assistant Professor of Geographic Information Sciences at Southwestern University .

items.title: Diva? “Maybe I need a little more of that in myself”: Pegula and Andreeva, the WTA Finals ‘divas’, meet for the first ti
paras: A week after being caught on a hot mic calling Mirra Andreeva “a diva”, Jessica Pegula faces the Russian for the first time in the first semi-final of the WTA Finals in Indian Wells on Saturday. It will be their first match on the tour.
“We’ve only practiced with each other twice, and we’ve never played,” Pegula said ahead of the semi-final. “I feel like we’re still a little unfamiliar with each other’s games.”

The remarks were picked up by the courtside microphones after a practice session between the two players, livestreamed on the WTA’s YouTube channel. Pegula, talking to her coach Mark Knowles, also criticised Andreeva’s coach, Conchita Martinez. The WTA removed the footage and apologised for failing to tell players the microphones were on. Andreeva posted a photo of them from the tournament photoshoot captioned “DIVAS”, and Pegula replied: “Divas in Chanel.”

items.title: Aryna Sabalenka appears to have a big problem developing which has emerged once again at the WTA Finals
paras: Aryna Sabalenka’s 2026 season is over, and she will likely be glad of it. After all, having started the year as the world number one and heavy favourite to compete for all four Grand Slams, she will instead end it without a single major title.

The highlight of her campaign came when the Belarusian completed the Sunshine Double, winning both Indian Wells and Miami back-to-back. It marked a vital bounce back after losing the Australian Open final, and suggested to the rest of the WTA Tour that she would not go out without a fight.

Sadly, this would represent the last piece of silverware Aryna Sabalenka would win in 2026, with her exit from the WTA Finals round robin representing a dire end to an underwhelming year. When Elena Rybakina withdrew from the WTA Finals , many felt this was a golden opportunity for Sabalenka.

items.title: Alcaraz and Ferrero reunite with a hug in Turin, almost a year after their split
paras: Carlos Alcaraz and Juan Carlos Ferrero greeted each other with a handshake and a hug in Turin on Saturday, their first public meeting since they stopped working together. Carlos Alcaraz and Juan Carlos Ferrero have met again, and it went well.

On Saturday in Turin, on the eve of the Nitto ATP Finals, the Spaniard and his former coach greeted each other with a handshake and a brief hug, in a scene filmed by Spanish outlet AS . It was their first public meeting since they stopped working together, almost a year ago.

The reunion took place during a public practice session, where Alcaraz was hitting with Ben Shelton, the American Ferrero now coaches. Alcaraz walked over to Ferrero and the team members standing by the net, and their hug drew an ovation from a crowd fully aware of what it was witnessing.

items.title: Seventeen Tournaments, Fifteen Champions: Is the WTA Tour Becoming Impossible to Predict?
paras: November 14, 2026 By Jack Beatnik Featured , Opinion , WTA Seventeen Tournaments, Fifteen Champions: Is the WTA Tour Becoming Impossible to Predict? Apparently, the WTA Tour has decided that allowing somebody to win more than one of these tournaments is becoming rather excessive.
Elena Rybakina managed it twice, winning Stuttgart and Ningbo . Mirra Andreeva also collected two, triumphing in Adelaide and Linz.

Diana Shnaider finished the season by winning Tokyo and the remaining trophies were scattered among an assortment of established players, emerging talents and occasional surprise champions. It is an extraordinary distribution of titles but does it mean women’s tennis has become more unpredictable? Or does it reveal something about how the leading players are increasingly organizing their seasons? The answer is way more interesting than the raw numbers suggest.

Friendships are built by repeated contact, not by being liked
items.hook: This is the single most useful fact in the whole guide.
paras: Studies of primary-school classrooms found that children seated next to each other were far more likely to become friends than children seated across the room. When teachers changed the seating, new friendships formed with the new neighbours.

So the engine is: same place, same people, same activity, over and over. The day at the yo-yo bar followed by basketball is that engine working - shared activity changed how the other boy treated him. It was not luck.
items.do: Pick one activity he already likes and commit to it weekly for a full term.

items.title: Keep the proximity - change the watching
items.hook: Your instinct is half right, and the other half matters.
paras: You are right that being around the group matters: children nominate as friends the children they see and interact with most. 'Out of sight, out of mind' is real for acquaintances.

But guidance written for schools is blunt: merely remaining beside a group is not friendship. A child who hovers is read as a bystander rather than a player, and it holds him in the one-down position. Watching has a use - but only as the first twenty seconds of joining in, never as the endpoint.
items.do: Keep telling him to stay near the group. Add: 'then take a job in the game'.

items.title: Teach 'watch, then blend'
items.hook: The best way to join a game is not to ask.
paras: Most of us were told to walk up and say 'Can I play?' But that makes everyone stop and look at him, and makes 'no' very easy.

The better sequence, used by people who study play: watch for about twenty seconds to learn the game and where the line is, then slide into the action without stopping it. Take the end of the line. Stand in the outfield. Pick up the ball and pass it back.
items.do: Rehearse it at home in five minutes. Ask him to name the 'easiest job' in each game.

items.title: Host one friend at a time - this is the biggest lever you control
items.hook: The child who invites is rarely short of friends.
paras: Pick a child he has had fun with in the last month, not someone he admires from afar. Invite one person for one to two hours. Put away anything precious, have two activities ready, start with a snack, and let the guest choose sometimes.
Keep it short and end while they are both still enjoying it. Then leave a few weeks before inviting the same child again, so the invitation can come back to him.
items.do: Text one parent this week and set a date for the school holidays.

items.title: Ask the teacher one specific question
items.hook: Teachers see the playground. Ask them to name names.
paras: Ask two things: who does he play well with, and could he be seated near them or paired with them for group work?
Seating is one of the few levers that reliably creates new friendships, and it is invisible to the children - no one has to know it was arranged.
items.do: Email the teacher this week with those two questions.

items.title: Do not push into a group that is rejecting him
items.hook: Here the advice is the opposite of persistence.
paras: Where a group is actively excluding him, the guidance is to back off - when you back off from people, they can move towards you. Put his energy into two or three other children instead of one closed circle.
Friends in more than one place - school, a club, family friends - also make him far less vulnerable when one group turns cold.
items.do: Help him list three children outside the difficult group he could get to know.

items.title: One or two good friends is the goal - not popularity
paras: Kids need one or two good friends. You do not need to worry about him being the most popular child in the class.
His warmth and kindness are already the raw material. Treat this as coaching a skill, not fixing a fault - if he feels like a project, he will resist.
items.do: Say his strengths out loud, often. Confidence is what carries a child into a group.

items.title: Playing and talking with girls is normal and good
items.hook: Children believe gender matters far more than it actually does.
paras: In one large classroom experiment, simply seating boys and girls next to each other doubled how often they became friends.
Girls' play tends to build conversation, turn-taking and inventing games together; boys' play builds bigger, faster group play. Being good at both widens his circle.
items.do: No action needed. Just do not let him think it is odd.

items.title: When to get more help
items.hook: Ordinary friendship difficulty is not a disorder.
paras: Get more support if he becomes reluctant to go to school, is persistently distressed, has changes in sleep or appetite, or says it is happening all the time and he cannot make it stop.
Start with his teacher, then the school counsellor, then your GP for a referral. Kids Helpline is free and open 24/7 on 1800 55 1800, for children and for parents.
items.do: Save Kids Helpline in your phone: 1800 55 1800.
